SUMMARYExecutive summary: three patterns to plan around

Three patterns to plan around

The report separates what the visuals show from how we might respond on match day.

01

Pressure the outlet

Lost defensive-third duels cluster on the right side of the report's pitch.

Possible responseTest a coordinated touchline press and cover the inside pass.
02

Manage pressing risk

Final-third recoveries suggest an aggressive counterpressing footprint.

Possible responseIf the first line is beaten, attack the space left behind.
03

Deny central access

Taylor leads the shown finishing metrics; Henderson leads listed through-pass volume.

Possible responseScreen central receivers before the final pass is played.
Evidence standard. Zone charts indicate location and volume—not causality, intent, or repeatability across opponents.

ADAPTATIONSPart II: formation shifts and match-state response

How shape changes generated momentum

The second part of the analysis links formation shifts to the outcomes in the AZ and PSV clips. Evidence standard: formation boards indicate role occupation and match-state trends, not exact touch locations or every off-ball adjustment.

01 · Rebalance the midfield

Ajax use role and line changes to improve central support and stay closer to the second ball.

RESPONSE Track the pivot drop and the next midfielder jumping beyond the ball.

02 · Change the front-line height

The attacking line becomes less flat, creating better distances for link play and deeper box access.

RESPONSE Watch the striker pin plus the runner arriving underneath.

03 · Use game state to lock control

Against PSV, Ajax later protect the lead with a more conservative structure and narrower central spacing.

RESPONSE Prepare one plan for the chase phase and another for the lead-protection phase.

Tactical adaptations 01: AZ comeback phase

Tactical readout

Midfield balanceIMPROVED
Support distanceSHORTER
Box accessBETTER
Rest defenceSTABLE

Finding

The shift compresses the distance from the pivot line to the attack, giving Ajax cleaner support for the next pass and better access into the equalizer phase.

Coaching action

Track the role change, not just the base formation. The key gain comes from better support underneath the front line and clearer links into the final third.

▶ clip 10 ▶ clip 11 ▶ clip 12

Tactical adaptations 02: a tactical movement can change the result

Readout

The structure matters because of the movement it unlocks: width to stretch the block, support beneath the first pass, and an extra arrival attacking the decisive zone.

Coaching action

Use the formation board to predict the run pattern, then confirm the trigger on video. Tactical movement, not the formation label alone, creates the result.

Tactical adaptations 03: PSV late phase

Game-state effect

Back lineFIVE
MidfieldNARROWER
Wide playersDEEPER
Central accessREDUCED

Finding

Once Ajax move into the 5-4-1, the priority shifts from chance creation to protecting the box, narrowing central distances, and managing the lead.

Coaching action

Expect the wing-back and wide-mid recovery. Prepare switches of play and second-phase circulation to move the block before crossing.

▶ clip 13

Four Part II priorities for the opposition meeting

01

Read the shape trigger

Press when the ball travels wide and Ajax begin to rebalance around the pivot.

02

Track the role change

Identify when the winger tucks inside or the midfielder jumps ahead of the ball.

03

Attack the transition window

If Ajax commit to the press or the chase phase, look for the space behind the first line.

04

Plan for both game states

Prepare one response for the comeback shape and another for the late lead-protection block.

Validation required. Confirm the exact minute bands, player availability, and whether the same triggers repeat across a larger sample.

MATCH PLANFour priorities for the opposition meeting

Four priorities for the opposition meeting

Translate scouting patterns into testable pressing and defensive cues.

01

Trigger on the flank

Apply pressure as the ball travels wide. Lock the inside pass before committing the second presser.

FROM BUILD-UP
02

Cover the pressing exit

When Ajax press high, prepare a forward option beyond the first pressure line.

FROM PRESS
03

Track the finishers

Deny Taylor clean central reception and stay connected to Edvardsen's box movements.

FROM FINISHING
04

Screen the initiator

Prioritize Henderson's body orientation and through-ball opportunities in the central lane.

FROM THROUGH PASSES
Validation required. Confirm sample period, pitch orientation and event coverage; use supporting video to validate each trigger.
EVIDENCEWhat the report claims, and what it does not

Evidence standard and open checks

What the report claims

  • Where Ajax lost own-third duels, and who, on the sample shown.
  • Where final-third recoveries cluster on the source pitch.
  • Which players lead the shown finishing and through-pass tables.
  • Possible responses, to be tested.

What it does not claim

  • Causality or intent: zone charts show location and volume only.
  • Repeatability across opponents or a season-long rate.
  • Stable finishing efficiency: event counts and xG are sample-specific.
